chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Ibn al-Qaddah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you has intercourse, let him not approach her as the bird approaches [its food], but let him stay [in the act] and linger.' Some of them said: 'And let him be patient/stay.'

key_terms.وَلْيَتَلَبَّثْ: and let him be patient/stay (variant reading)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for marital intimacy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith emphasizes the Sunnah of foreplay and lingering during marital intimacy, contrasting the 'bird-like' haste with deliberate, affectionate presence. The variant reading 'yatalabbath' underscores the virtue of patience and savoring the moment, reflecting the Shia emphasis on mutual pleasure and emotional connection as acts of worship. This guidance transforms physical union into a spiritual bond, encouraging men to prioritize their wives' satisfaction as a form of kindness (ihsan).
